note: Main inputs read from g4/12: research staff (faculty + fellows + PhD students) and deflated current costs, t-1.
One frontier per year: each year is compared only with itself, so a fall in recent Scopus counts cannot penalise 2023 against 2021.

R6 removes single university-year observations, not universities as such: 13 observations of 6 universities (Bologna; Milano; Milano Politecnico; Padova; Roma La Sapienza; Torino). Bologna and Milano and Roma La Sapienza are flagged in every year, so they leave the sample entirely.

R7 removes all years of Napoli L'Orientale, Siena Stranieri and Perugia Stranieri as a sensitivity check for possible output-coverage differences. Scopus also indexes books and monographs; a coverage error in this dataset has not been established. See Elsevier's Scopus content policy and selection page.

R8 uses faculty, PhD students and deflated costs as three separate inputs (p + q = 4). With one more input DEA mechanically finds more efficient units: each extra dimension adds directions in which a unit can be undominated, so the share of efficient units rises and scores move towards 1 even if the technology is unchanged. Fellows are excluded here (they are in the main input and in R5). Four separate labour and cost inputs (p + q = 5) are not used: with n = 183 the DEA convergence rate n^(2/(p+q+1)) becomes slow and too many units would lie on the frontier for the comparison to be informative.
R9 is the main version until 28 November 2026 (faculty only + deflated costs). Its Spearman correlation is the rank correlation between the new and the old main scores.
Spearman correlations use the university-years common to the version and the main frontier; scores of different frontiers are not directly comparable in levels.
